Let \(p=2027\) and \(q=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). We work modulo \(p\).

A useful coefficient identity is

\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k=\binom{-1/2}{k}(-8)^k.
\]

Since \(k\le p-1\), the denominator \(k!\) is invertible modulo \(p\). Also

\[
-\frac12 \equiv \frac{p-1}{2}=q \pmod p.
\]

Thus, for \(0\le k<p\),

\[
\binom{-1/2}{k}\equiv \binom{q}{k}\pmod p,
\]

where \(\binom{q}{k}=0\) for \(k>q\). Therefore

\[
S \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{q} k(-8)^k\binom{q}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Now use

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{q} kx^k\binom{q}{k}
= x\frac{d}{dx}(1+x)^q
= xq(1+x)^{q-1}.
\]

With \(x=-8\),

\[
S \equiv (-8)q(1-8)^{q-1}
= -8q(-7)^{q-1}\pmod p.
\]

We need \((-7)^{q-1}\). By Euler’s criterion,

\[
(-7)^q\equiv \left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)\pmod{2027}.
\]

Compute the Legendre symbol:

\[
2027\equiv 3\pmod 4 \implies \left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)=-1.
\]

Also

\[
2027\equiv 4\pmod 7,
\]

and since \(q=1013\) is odd,

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
= -\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
= -\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
= -1.
\]

Hence

\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)
=
\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=(-1)(-1)=1.
\]

So \((-7)^q\equiv 1\), and therefore

\[
(-7)^{q-1}\equiv (-7)^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since

\[
(-7)\cdot 579=-4053\equiv 1\pmod{2027},
\]

we have \((-7)^{-1}\equiv 579\). Thus

\[
S\equiv -8\cdot 1013\cdot 579\pmod{2027}.
\]

Now

\[
-8\cdot 1013=-8104\equiv 4\pmod{2027},
\]

so

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
